newsitem.title: SWEDEN: No Moody's upgrade seen for Sweden - paper.
newsitem.headline: No Moody's upgrade seen for Sweden - paper.

text.p: Sweden's credit ratings are not ready to be upgraded despite improved state finances, Swedish business newspaper Dagens Industri on Thursday quoted a spokeswoman from U.S. credit ratings agency Moody's as saying.
"It can become a problem for Sweden to continue the fiscal tightening as it comes into an election period," Moody's Sweden analyst Kristin Lindow told the newspaper.
The Swedish political situation was uncertain in 1997, with only one year remaining before the next general election.
"We don't feel certain that the government will manage to keep the budget deficit down because of political pressure," the newspaper quoted her as saying.
Moody's instead favours neighboring Finland, to whose Finnish markka-denominated debt it assigned a first-time Aaa rating earlier this month.

Moody's also raised the sovereign ceiling for Finland's foreign currency debt to Aa1 from Aa2. As a result, the agency upgraded foreign currency-denominated bonds and notes issued by Finland to Aa1 from Aa2.
Sweden lacks Finland's political unity when it comes to rationalisation of state finance, the newspaper quoted Lindow as saying. This year would be crucial, she told the newspaper.
"We are looking for significant signals before we dare to recommend that Sweden's credit ratings should be examined for a possible upgrade," Lindow said, according to the newspaper.
Sweden's state finance situation was "impressive," Dagens Industri quoted Lindow as saying.
In January 1995, Moody's downgraded Sweden's long-term foreign currency debt rating to Aa3 from Aa2.
